brief_summary: Five-row comparison table of legend methods (double-shot, dye-sub, pad print, UV print, laser) across three columns: where the legend lives, colour rule, wear. Each row carries a small slab glyph showing the legend's depth — full-thickness column (double-shot, ochre), shallow stain (dye-sub, ochre), film above the surface (pad/UV), notch cut into the surface (laser). 'In the plastic' and 'in the surface' are emphasised in ochre; 'wears off' in the warm-red caution token.
data_sources: how-keycaps-are-made-deep-dive.mdx § 'Double-shot: the legend is a second shot' — 'makes the legend out of plastic rather than putting it on plastic' / 'the doubleshot legends will never fade'

how-keycaps-are-made-deep-dive.mdx § 'Dye-sublimation: the legend is a stain' — 'A legend can only be darker than the cap beneath it' / 'The workaround is reverse dye-sub' / 'The legend cannot flake, and it wears at the same rate as the cap around it'

how-keycaps-are-made-deep-dive.mdx § 'Pad printing, UV printing, laser' — 'handles any colour on any base, and it wears through within months on the home row because the ink is a film sitting on the plastic' / 'UV-cured ink in full colour, which is how multicolour novelties get made on top of double-shot bodies'

how-keycaps-are-made-deep-dive.mdx § 'Pad printing, UV printing, laser' — 'a pale mark on black ABS, a lighter recess on dark PBT — and laser-filled variants ablate a recess and flood it with paint. The recess is permanent; the fill wears like pad print.'
